For seniors to
● adopt an active and healthier lifestyle
through physical activity, volunteerism,
● foster greater social connectedness and
mental wellness.
We hope to achieve these objectives
● To provide a holistic approach towards overall wellness
● To encourage seniors to experience different activities that enhance
their physical, mental and social wellness
● To attract seniors with different interests to come to AAC

when you plan AAP.

We are expected to conduct communal dining once a week

● Spending time

AACs will serve as a key go-to point for social and health matters to seniors and their caregivers.
• AACs will be the first-stop for seniors for their social and health-related matters.
• AACs may not render all the services as required by the seniors.

Befriending and Buddying Information and Referral 2S
2S: Social Connector & Community Screening
Healthier SG was launched on 1 July 2023. As part of Healthier SG’s initiatives, AACs shall serve as:
1. A Social Connector to help seniors follow through with social and lifestyle interventions as
recommended by their family doctors.
2. Community nodes to provide assistance in Community Screening (e.g. vital signs monitoring) for
seniors who have been advised by their family doctor to do so.
*Note: These services are not boundary-specific.
The services may be rendered through referrals of seniors, or seniors who walk into AAC to request for
assistance.
Should your AAC receive a referral from the RHSes/PCN HQs for seniors that are residing outside of your
service boundary, this means that:
i. The senior’s current postal code of residence is not being served by any AACs; and
ii. Your AAC is the nearest AAC to the senior’s place of residence.
Your AAC are expected to provide 2S assistances to these referred seniors.

Active Ageing Collaborations – GUI Capability Building Funding, KPIs, and Reporting
AACs to further increase engagement of seniors with a greater diversity of programming
in the community by tapping on Ground-Up Initiatives (GUI)
1. GUI is a new yearly opt-in funding stream for AACs (~$45k per FY). This amount will be disbursed upfront as part of
programme funding, AACs are given flexibility to utilise funding as long as GUI KPIs are met.
Objectives:
a) ​Provide a greater diversity and vibrancy to programming in the community by leveraging ground energy and resources
(e.g. volunteers).
b) AACs as anchors in the region; GUIs to augment AAC in serving localised social/health needs of seniors.
What qualifies as GUI that AACs can work with/channel funding to:
1. Proposed activity/programme should serve seniors in partner AACs’ assigned service boundary and bring seniors out
of their house for some form of in-person activity and not solely providing space/venue for AAC usage only.
2. External organisations or individuals/interest groups that are not from AAC/AACs’ parent organisation1, clusters or
other government agencies (e.g. HPB, NParks).
3. Proposed activity/programme is not concurrently receiving funding from another government agency.
1Parent organisation: direct organisationthat oversees the AAC operations

Active Ageing Collaborations – GUI Capability Building Funding, KPIs, and Reporting
GUI Administration
1. AACs will be held to following GUI KPIs:
KPI 1: Total number of sessions delivered by all the GUI partners under the AAC, in the FY
• Target = 24 sessions
KPI 2: Total number of unique seniors to be served (i.e., brought out for activities) by all the GUI partners under the AAC, in the FY
• Target = 160 unique seniors
2. GUI indicators to be reported in AACs’ progress report:
• GUI partner and programme details
• Number of sessions organised and unique seniors served
• Participant feedback
3. AAC will be subject to clawback of GUI funding:
• 100% if AACs did not have any GUI partners and activities, or
• 50% if AACs have GUI partners/activities but did not meet all GUI-related KPIs.
4. The same senior reported for GUI KPI can also be counted towards AACs' KPI 1 if the GUI activity is:
• Co-organised by the GUI partner and AAC
• Listed in Repository of Evidence-Informed and Criteria Cleared AAPs
